title: Make the Property Explorer valuation label say what the value actually is
missionPremise: CTX-B1 (legacy-design-tools PR #650) implements operator ruling A1: a served dollar carries a valueBasis derived from the row rather than asserted by a constant. It reached three of four serve paths and NAMED the fourth as out of its scope rather than silently dropping it. The fourth is the Property Explorer label, in hauska-map. This lane is that fourth path. Source: the dispatch body, and gh pr view 650 read live at CP1.
completionPredicate: A fixture carrying valueBasis "stratmap-redistributed" renders neither the string "Tax-assessed value" nor county-appraisal-roll wording; that assertion was observed FAILING against a build that renders what main renders, and PASSING after. A genuine county-assessed fixture is unchanged at both. The tax-valuation-paint.ts comment no longer asserts every figure comes from the county appraisal district. PE typecheck and the PE suite terminate green. A PR is open and not merged. ALL MET.
scopeBasis: hauska-map only, per the dispatch. legacy-design-tools was READ and never written (gh pr view 650, gh pr diff 650, and lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/landuse.ts) to establish the wire contract and the StratMap row shape rather than infer them. hauska-factory and hauska-engine were not touched; two other lanes were live in hauska-factory (CTX-B2, CTX-B3) and this lane was the only one in hauska-map. No deploy, no Cloud Build, no Cloud Run job, no bake, no publish, no walk — the integration seat owns every deploy and execution.

theQuestionAndTheAnswer.asked: Decide and justify how the panel should express the two bases so a viewer can tell them apart without being told the value is missing. Name at least two candidate treatments and say why you rejected the one you did not take.

candidatesConsidered.name: Provenance chip / Sources disclosure only, heading untouched
candidatesConsidered.why: Two independent kills. (a) It is behind a click, and the dispatch's own framing is what a viewer who never opens a tooltip takes away. (b) It does not work at all: taxValuationFacetFromSheet maps a present fact through present(display) and CardFacet<string> has no provenance field, so this row's provenance sibling is dropped before the card and never reaches the disclosure. A chip-only treatment would have rendered NOTHING. It is the treatment that looks like the house rule and is in fact the artifact-that-does-nothing defect class ENFORCEMENT.md opens with: it would have passed review and enforced nothing.

candidatesConsidered.name: Row heading only
candidatesConsidered.verdict: REJECTED as sufficient, ADOPTED in part
candidatesConsidered.why: A changed heading says THAT something differs and never WHAT. It cannot express the difference between four non-county states without turning the row's name into a status field. And the natural heading words for the stratmap case (estimated, modelled, approximate) are the market-opinion vocabulary A-103 item 5 and Masters 06 forbid. Adopted only for the narrow job of removing a false claim.

candidatesConsidered.name: Keep the ruled heading on every parcel, carry the basis in a face line only
candidatesConsidered.why: It leaves 'Tax-assessed value' standing over a dollar that is not this county's tax assessment. The dispatch names that heading as one of the three false statements. A true line under a false heading is still a card with a false statement on its face.

candidatesConsidered.name: CHOSEN: heading and face line, each doing one job
candidatesConsidered.why: The heading's only job is to stop making a claim the row cannot support. The face line, in the same slot and at the same weight as the honest-absence basis line the card already ships, carries the statement. The heading is not asked to explain and the line is not asked to be the row's name.

theQuestionAndTheAnswer.whatAViewerWhoNeverTapsTakesAway: The row is named differently AND names a different source, both in plain text on the card face, at 11.5px directly under the amounts, with no hover, tap or tooltip. Side by side: 'Recorded value / Market $6,506,490 ... / From the Texas StratMap statewide parcel file.' against 'Tax-assessed value / Market $1,884,580 ... Assessed $1,884,580 / From Caldwell County's own appraisal-roll export.' Each is a true, complete statement of what the number is and where it came from.

absentValueBasisDecision.renders: The `unstated` state: heading 'Recorded value', face line 'This record does not state which source the figure came from.', provenance sourceLabel '<County> County parcel record, source not stated', data-value-basis="unstated".
absentValueBasisDecision.why: It is a decision, not a default. Reading an absent basis as `county-assessed` writes the claim 'someone checked and it is the county's' onto a record where nothing checked — the same lie as converting an unaccounted cell to absent-verified to clear a gate. Reading it as `stratmap-redistributed` asserts a specific lineage on equally no evidence and would silently downgrade every older baked payload in the corpus. Absent, zero and unmeasured are three different states and this is the third.
absentValueBasisDecision.reachableAndTested: Yes. A payload whose rails carry dollars and no valueBasis (an older bake, which is what most live payloads are today) resolves here, and there is a render-level test and four unit tests for it.

fiveStatesNotTwo.why: valueBasis has two members on the wire. The resolved basis has five, because three are properties of the READ rather than of the wire, and each is a state a shorter implementation would have collapsed into county-assessed.

states.county-assessed: the county's own appraisal export. Heading unchanged per A-103 item 5.
states.stratmap-redistributed: the free public TxGIO/StratMap statewide land-parcels file (LAND_VALUE / IMP_VALUE / MKT_VALUE).
states.unstated: no rail carried a basis. See above.
states.unrecognised: a rail carried a token this build cannot name. Deliberately NOT folded into unstated: the record stated a source and the reader failed, which is contract drift this surface must show rather than absorb. The raw token is printed so it is diagnosable from a screenshot.
states.mixed: the rails disagree. legacy-design-tools resolves one basis per parcel and stamps all four rails, but that is an invariant of NEW bakes, not a property of payloads already in the store. First-rail-wins would round off exactly the finding worth having (contract section 5: two numbers that should agree and do not is a free finding).

fiveStatesNotTwo.noneIsDormant: Each of the five is reachable by payload shape and each has a render-level test and unit tests. The suite asserts every basis produces a non-empty sentence and that all five sentences are DISTINCT, so no state can silently become a synonym for another.

theLineRendersOnCountyAssessedToo: Deliberate and load-bearing. If the line appeared only for the non-county bases, a row that lost it to a rendering bug, a stale bake or a future refactor would be indistinguishable from a genuine county figure, and silence would read as the strongest claim on the card. Always occupying the slot makes the county case a positive statement rather than a default-by-silence.

instrumentDefectsIFoundInMyOwnTests: Copy assertions ran against raw markup, so a row that rendered 'From Caldwell County's own appraisal-roll export.' failed a toContain for that exact string — React escapes the apostrophe to '. Caught ONLY because the county-assessed control was pre-registered as must-pass. Fixed: copy assertions run on tag-stripped, entity-decoded visible text.
The 'no market-opinion vocabulary' regex matched data-testid="valuation-basis" — the test tripping over its own hook. It could never have passed. Fixed the same way.

A VACUOUS PASS: 'renders different basis lines' compared a McLennan render against a Caldwell render, so the lines differed because the county names did, not because the bases did. It passed against the stubbed build, where both bases produced the identical claim. Found by reading the stub run's PASS list rather than only its FAIL list. Fixed: both fixtures render under one county name, and it now fails at the stub with the rest.

Worth stating plainly: two of the twenty failures in the first run were the instrument lying, and reporting '20 failures, violation confirmed' would have been wrong in a way that looked right. The pre-registered falsifier is what caught it.

designFindingFromTheAfterRun.finding: After the stubs came off, exactly one assertion still failed. The stratmap line read 'From the Texas StratMap statewide parcel file, not McLennan County's own appraisal-roll export.' — it contained the forbidden phrase, as a denial.
designFindingFromTheAfterRun.resolution: Changed the COPY rather than loosening the check. Three reasons in order of weight: the dispatch's criterion is a ruling to follow, not a constraint to reinterpret once inconvenient; a substring check cannot tell attribution from denial and rewriting it would have made it presence-shaped and fragile; and on an 11.5px muted line the phrase a skim-reader lands on in 'From A, not B' is B, which here is the false claim this lane exists to remove.
designFindingFromTheAfterRun.result: The stratmap line is the positive statement alone: 'From the Texas StratMap statewide parcel file.' A new assertion forbids the word 'appraisal' in ANY non-county-assessed line, denial included, so it cannot drift back.
designFindingFromTheAfterRun.whatWasGivenUp: The explicit correction of a reader's prior expectation. A reader must notice that both the heading and the source line changed rather than being told so. Deliberate trade, not an oversight.

LESSON: A `FactPresentation.provenance` string in PE's InspectCard is DEMOTED into the collapsed SourcesDisclosure, not rendered on the card face. And the taxValuation row's provenance sibling is dropped even earlier: taxValuationFacetFromSheet maps a present fact through present(display), and CardFacet<string> has no provenance field. Any future 'put it in the provenance chip' answer for that row renders NOTHING. The face-level carrier is FactRow's basis-line slot (data-testid=layer-absence-basis, marginTop 3, fontSize 11.5), which is the house pattern for a statement that must not be behind a tap.

A violation run is far stronger as a COMMIT than as a transcript. Land the plumbing with the behaviour-changing function stubbed to today's behaviour, run the suite red, commit that, then destub. Anyone can `git checkout <sha>` and reproduce the failure, and it proves the test is not vacuous. Costs one extra commit.

React escapes apostrophes to `'` in renderToStaticMarkup output. Copy assertions against raw markup fail on any string containing one. Assert on tag-stripped, entity-decoded VISIBLE TEXT; keep raw-markup assertions for data attributes and test ids only.

A negative regex over rendered markup can match the test's own `data-testid`. `/valuation|worth|estimate/i` matched `data-testid="valuation-basis"`. Such an assertion can never pass and reports a violation no viewer could see.

Read the PASS list of a violation run, not only the FAIL list. A test comparing two fixtures that differ in TWO ways (here: county name and basis) passes for the wrong reason and would have shipped as coverage. Hold every variable but the one under test constant.

'From A, not B' is good explanation and bad micro-copy when B is a false claim you are removing: on a small muted line the skim-read lands on B. Carry the non-claim in the heading and keep the line positive.

apps/property-explorer typecheck needs `pnpm --filter @hauska/map-renderer build` first. Without it, 9 TS2307 errors on @hauska/map-renderer appear and look like your change broke something. They are on main too.
DEAD-END: Overloading `Provenance.method` (a free-form `string | null`) to carry the valuation basis across the sheet boundary. Rejected: it is a sentinel overload of a field documented as 'derivation method', and a later reader cannot tell a basis from a method. The contract amendment was the right cost.

Carrying the resolved basis and an unrecognised producer token in ONE string field on the contract. Rejected: the resolution vocabulary (unstated/unrecognised/mixed) and the producer's token space collide the moment a producer ships a tier named like a resolution member. Two flat fields instead.

Deriving the county name inside InspectCard from `baked.county`, which renders as 'Bastrop County (48021)'. Rejected: parsing a fact back out of another rendered string is how a display bug becomes a provenance bug. Composed at sheet-to-card-model instead, the last place the county name exists as a field.

Changing `cadProvenance` (the shared cad-roll provenance) to reflect valueBasis. Rejected: it is shared with APN, situs and land use, and valueBasis is evidence about the DOLLAR fields only (derived from assessed_value presence). A control broader than its claim is the worse defect.
